invaders.description: Whether the periodic raid generator runs. With this off a room's harvest budget is cleared on every tick so no raiding party spawns. A room which banked a budget before this was switched off may still see one last raid.

deposits.description: Whether the periodic deposit generator (mods/modern/deposit) runs. Off by default: the placement intent is dropped, so no new deposit is ever put down. Deposits already in the world keep being harvested and decay on schedule, and their decay no longer triggers a refill. Set to true for vanilla placement.

powerBanks.description: Whether the periodic power bank generator (mods/modern/powerbank) runs. Off by default: the placement intent is dropped, so no new bank is ever put down. Banks already in the world decay on schedule. Set to true for vanilla placement.

ruins.description: Whether a destroyed structure leaves a ruin behind. Off by default: a ruin never reaches the room -- the object handed to Room['#insertObject'] is dropped, so nothing is left to loot and nothing is left to decay. Covers combat and decay destruction and the two spawn intents (handover / abandoned base), whose ruins otherwise sit in the room for 100000 and 500000 ticks. No room blob format changes; the EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROYED log entry is still appended and tombstones are untouched. Set to true for vanilla ruins.

respawnCleanup.description: Whether the neutral structures a leaving player left behind are cleared out when they respawn. On by default: roads, containers and walls carry no owner, so the vanilla handover leaves them standing for good (a container never decays). A room the player owned or reserved is cleared outright; a room they only had creeps in is cleared only while no other player is standing in it. Container contents go with it and the destruction is logged. Power banks, deposits, portals and controllers are never touched. Set to false to leave the leftovers standing.

raceBrackets.description: Tick offsets after a landing which are recorded as race results, in game ticks (default 20000 and 40000). Each bracket stores one row per run -- RCL level, progress, control points, GCL -- and puts the run in a ranked set, which is what a leaderboard page reads. Offsets are ticks, so a paused shard freezes a race rather than voiding it. A result only lands while the player still holds the room at RCL 2 or above; a superseded run or a lost room simply stops scoring. Empty records nothing.

respawnAfter.description: How many ticks a run lasts before the server respawns the player, in game ticks (default 40000, i.e. the last bracket). A landing starts the clock; when it runs out the player is handed over exactly as if they had clicked respawn -- their objects are taken out of their rooms and the controllers released -- and no spawn is placed for them, so the next run starts from the landing they make themselves. Set to 0 to leave respawns to the player.

claimController.description: Whether creeps may claim neutral controllers. Off by default: Creep.claimController returns ERR_INVALID_TARGET before recording an intent, so no room can change hands. reserveController/attackController/upgradeController still work, and a new player's starting room is claimed through its own placeSpawn intent. Set to true to let players claim again.

closeCenterNine.description: Whether the sector cores (each sector's center room plus its eight neighbours, the central 3x3) are closed on every service start. On by default. Closing drops the room from the world's open-room list, which Game.map.getRoomStatus() reports as `closed`; nothing inside the room is deleted and no other room is touched. The rooms are read from the world's own sector records. Set to false on a shard which wants its cores playable.

wallSectorCores.description: Whether the sector cores (each sector's center room plus its eight neighbours) are painted solid on service start: every tile of those nine rooms becomes wall, together with the facing edge of each room around them, because crossing a room border is the step which has to be refused. On unless set to false. Terrain is the only thing written -- no object is deleted, no room blob is rewritten, and the sector record on the center room survives, so deposit and power bank placement keep working. The world's original terrain blob is kept under speedrun/terrainBackup so the wall can be lifted. Takes effect on the service start after the one which writes it.

uniformRooms.description: Whether every room of each sector's interior is overwritten with one shared terrain. Off by default. The template is generated the way generate-room generates a room -- wall layouts 1-28 (uniformTerrainType), swamp layouts 0-14 (uniformSwampType), the same cellular-automaton fill and smoothing -- with one change: every side is opened with the same centred run (uniformExitWidth) instead of the exits the neighbours happen to have, so two rooms built from it share a border tile for tile and the whole grid walks through. A layout which comes out in several pieces is repaired rather than rerolled, so all 28 connect on all four sides. Terrain is the only thing written: no room blob is rewritten and no object is read, moved or deleted, so a source a wall landed next to is reported in the service log rather than moved. Rooms around a core keep the face which looks at it shut, and the highway ring keeps its own terrain except for the tiles of a face which looks at a covered room (uniformRingEdges). The template is generated once and stored, so a restart, a rollback or a redeploy does not change the world; editing a layout key generates a new template and restamps the interior. The world's terrain before the first stamp is kept under speedrun/terrainBackup. Takes effect on the service start after the one which writes it.

uniformTerrainType.description: Wall layout for uniformRooms, 1-28: the terrain-type of the generate-room command. Omitted means a random layout, which is rolled once and kept. A layout which leaves the room in several pieces is repaired -- the exits carved into the main region and the pockets walled off -- rather than rerolled, so every layout connects on all four sides.

uniformSwampType.description: Swamp layout for uniformRooms, 1-14, or 0 for no swamp at all: the swamp-type of the generate-room command. Omitted means a random layout, which is rolled once and kept.

uniformExitWidth.description: How many tiles wide the opening on every side of the uniformRooms template is. Even, so the opening is centred and symmetric about both axes; the same run on all four sides is what lines two rooms up across a border.

uniformRingEdges.description: Whether the highway ring's inward faces are opened to match the uniformRooms template. On by default: a room at the edge of the interior would otherwise advertise an exit the ring seals, and a creep walking out of it would be handed into a wall. Only the tiles of a face which looks at a covered room are written -- the rest of the ring, its own lane ends included, is left exactly as it is.
